metadata.Description:
- This course introduces the key steps involved in the data mining pipeline, including data understanding, data preprocessing, data warehousing, data modeling, interpretation and evaluation, and real-world applications.
- Students will learn the general concepts of data mining along with basic methodologies and applications. Then dive into one subfield in data mining: pattern discovery. Learn in-depth concepts, methods, and applications of pattern discovery in data mining. This courser will introduce methods for pattern-based classification and some interesting applications of pattern discovery. It also provides you the opportunity to learn skills and content to practice and engage in scalable pattern discovery methods on massive transactional data, discuss pattern evaluation measures, and study methods for mining diverse kinds of patterns, sequential patterns, and sub-graph patterns.

metadata.Description: Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed industries around the world, and has the potential to radically alter the field of healthcare. The aim of this unit is to introducethe current and future applications of AI in healthcare with the goal of learning to bring AI technologies into the clinic safely and ethically. Students will be guided to analyze data on patient, such as diseases, medications, tests, or valuable health information, and get a sense of how AI could transform patient care and diagnoses.

metadata.Description: This speech processing course comprehensively explains how humans and machines generate, transmit, and process speech signals. The course covers speech production, phonetics, acoustic analysis, speech perception, speech recognition, natural language processing, and speech synthesis. Students will learn about the principles and algorithms behind various speech-processing techniques, including signal processing, machine learning, and deep learning. The course also covers speech processing applications in speech recognition, speech recognition, speech synthesis, and speech enhancement. Upon completing the course, students will have a solid foundation in speech processing and be equipped with the necessary skills to tackle real-world speech-processing problems.

clos.CLO Details: Gain a comprehensive understanding of fundamental principles in processing speech signals, covering digital signal processing (DSP) methods, feature extraction, and speech signal analysis

Develop expertise in speech recognition and synthesis, exploring and applying various algorithms for automatic speech recognition (ASR) and speech synthesis, including rule-based and statistical approaches
Apply relevant machine learning algorithms and models to address speech-processing challenges, including feature extraction, classification, and other tasks within the speech context
Acquire practical skills by using and implementing widely-used speech-processing tools, software, libraries, and frameworks, such as Praat, HTK, or other relevant platforms

Demonstrate the ability to assess speech-processing system performance, applying appropriate metrics to evaluate accuracy and efficiency in speech recognition and synthesis models. Critically analyze the strengths and limitations of various approaches

metadata.Description: Multimodal AI course aim on building AI systems that operate across modalities - vision, language, audio, video, 3D, and embodiment. The course frames multimodality through four core problems (representation, alignment, fusion, translation) and proceeds through cross-modal representations (CLIP, SigLIP, ImageBind), fusion architectures (cross-attention, Perceiver, Q-Former, gated cross-attention), vision-language and unified models (LLaVA, BLIP-2, Flamingo, Chameleon/Janus families), speech and audio, video and world models, 3D and embodied agents, multimodal reasoning / agents / RAG, evaluation (benchmark saturation, hallucination), efficiency and deployment, and safety/provenance/frontiers. Mathematical depth is assumed from the prerequisites (Deep Learning, Advanced Generative AI); this course focuses on architectures, training recipes, evaluation, and hands-on multimodal systems.

clos.CLO Details: Identify and characterize multimodal AI systems and the four core problems of multimodal machine learning - representation, alignment, fusion, and translation.
Build cross-modal representations using contrastive and self-supervised methods, and evaluate them via zero-shot transfer and cross-modal retrieval.
Design and implement fusion architectures (cross-attention, latent bottlenecks, connector modules) that combine heterogeneous modalities.
Apply vision-language and unified multimodal architectures (LLaVA, BLIP-2, Flamingo, and unified token/diffusion-transformer families) and instruction-tune them.
Apply multimodal techniques to non-image modalities - speech, audio, video, 3D, and embodied agents - and to cross-modal generation.
Engineer multimodal reasoning, agent, and retrieval systems, and address the input-size and latency challenges of deploying them.
Evaluate multimodal systems with appropriate benchmarks and protocols, recognizing saturation and the migrating frontier, and run hallucination and grounding diagnostics.
Analyze the safety, provenance, bias, and privacy issues specific to multimodal AI - deepfakes, watermarking, and biometric data.

metadata.Syllabus Name: Cloud for MLOps_Cloud cho hoạt động học máy
metadata.Time Allocation: 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
metadata.Description: This course provides students with practical knowledge and skills to design, deploy, and operate end-to-end MLOps pipelines on cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud). Students will master cloud-native data engineering (S3/GCS, Kafka, Dataflow, Glue), data versioning with DVC, feature stores (Feast, Vertex Feature Store), and scalable model training using distributed GPU/TPU clusters. The curriculum covers CI/CD for ML (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI), containerization with Docker, Kubernetes-based deployment (GKE/EKS/AKS), and production monitoring with Prometheus, Grafana, and cloud-native logging. Through hands-on labs and a final cloud-deployed project, students will gain comprehensive experience in building production-ready ML systems with automated monitoring, drift detection, and retraining pipelines, while addressing cost optimization, security, and compliance (GDPR, HIPAA).
metadata.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.
- Students are responsible for completing all exercises, assignments, 4 labs, and 2 process tests assigned by the instructor in class or at home, and submitting them on time.
- Students must complete a final group project (end-to-end MLOps pipeline on cloud) and submit a 4–6 page scientific paper describing the architecture, experiments, ops plan, and cost analysis.
- Laptops are to be used in class strictly for learning purposes.
- Students must promptly access the FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information.
metadata.Tools: Python, AWS (SageMaker, Lambda, ECR, GKE/EKS/AKS), Google Cloud (Vertex AI, Cloud Composer, GCR), Azure (Azure ML, ACR), Docker, Kubernetes, DVC, MLflow, Feast, TFX, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI, Terraform, Prometheus, Grafana, Evidently AI, FastAPI, TensorFlow Serving.
metadata.Note:
- The course adopts a practice oriented, PBL (project base learning) approach in which students progressively design, deploy, monitor, and maintain an end to end cloud native ML (Machine Learning) system throughout the semester.
- Students complete four hands on laboratory assignments focusing on cloud data versioning and orchestration, TFX pipelines and model validation, containerization and Kubernetes deployment, and monitoring with automated retraining. Labs are completed individually or in assigned teams and submitted before the specified deadlines.
- Two computer based multiple choice Progress Tests evaluate students' theoretical understanding of Cloud MLOps, cloud architecture, data engineering, MLOps pipelines, CI/CD, containerization, deployment, and monitoring concepts.
- Two Process Tests assess practical competencies through production-oriented scenarios, including incident response, drift detection, rollback strategies, model promotion, CI/CD execution, and deployment validation.
- The mandatory team based capstone project requires students to design and implement a complete cloud native MLOps solution, supported by an end-to-end pipeline, technical documentation, cost analysis, a scientific paper, and an in class presentation with a live demonstration.
- The final examination is an individual computer-based multiple choice test covering all major Cloud MLOps concepts and practices.
- The final course grade is calculated as follows: Progress Test 1 (10%), Progress Test 2 (10%), Lab 1 (7.5%), Lab 2 (7.5%), Lab 3 (7.5%), Lab 4 (7.5%), Process Test 1 (7.5%), Process Test 2 (7.5%), Final Project (20%), and Final Examination (10%).
- Completion Criteria: All assessments must score above 0, with a minimum Final Examination score of 4.0 and an overall course grade of 5.0.

clos.CLO Details: Understand core concepts, differences, and relationships among MLOps, DevOps, DataOps, and LLMOps (including RAG & Prompt Engineering basics); apply cloud architecture patterns for ML systems (ingestion, storage, deployment models) across major cloud platforms (AWS SageMaker, Azure ML, Vertex AI).

Design and implement cloud-based data engineering pipelines using cloud-native services (AWS Lambda/Step Functions/Glue, GCP Dataflow/Cloud Composer, Azure Data Factory) and implement feature store management solutions (Feast, Vertex/Azure Feature Store) for offline/online inference.

Apply experiment tracking tools (MLflow, WandB, SageMaker Experiments, Vertex Vizier) and data versioning principles using DVC with cloud remotes (S3/GCS/Azure) to ensure reproducibility, data lineage, and metadata management in ML experiments.
Design and build end-to-end TensorFlow Extended (TFX) and cloud native pipelines (including ExampleGen, Transform, Trainer, Evaluator, Publisher), establish model baselines, and handle concept drift.
Understand feature store concepts and implement feature management solutions using Feast, Vertex Feature Store, or Azure Feature Stores for offline/online inference on cloud.

Apply Docker containerization best practices, build containerized MLOps pipelines to deploy to cloud registries (ECR/GCR/ACR) and services (Cloud Run, ECS, GKE, AKS), and implement model serving patterns (TF Serving, FastAPI, Flask) with progressive delivery (blue-green, canary) and autoscaling (HPA/VPA).

Implement automated CI/CD pipelines for ML using GitHub Actions, Jenkins, or GitLab CI integrated with cloud services to automate model deployments, testing, and continuous validation in cloud environments.

Implement continuous model monitoring (Prometheus, Grafana, Cloud Monitoring) for data/concept drift, setup automated retraining triggers based on performance thresholds, and apply operational excellence principles (incident response, runbooks, rollback, data governance, GDPR, HIPAA, IAM).

Implement an end-to-end Cloud MLOps capstone project encompassing infrastructure setup, automated data pipelines, model tracking, cloud deployment, monitoring, automated retraining, and document it via a scientific/technical paper (4–6 pages) detailing architecture, experiments, ops plan, and cost analysis.
